followup_explanation:
This was a multi-turn-flavored, warm, good-faith analytical request — exactly the kind of collaborative, polite exchange Curlew self-reports as its top task family, and it edges out Willet on the relevant capability evals too.

Specifically:

1. **Capability fit.** The query is a structured analytical "walk me through opportunities and challenges" task, which leans on knowledge breadth and reasoning. Curlew leads on the relevant benchmarks (MMLU-Pro 80.3 vs 75.9, GPQA Diamond 62.5 vs 56.2, Arena-Hard 89.1 vs 83.2) and on the closest internal eval categories (Summarization 85.8 vs 80.6; Support Dialogue 86.2 vs 78.9). This isn't unconstrained creative invention — it has clear analytical structure — so Curlew's aversion to open-ended generative work isn't really triggered.

2. **Preference fit.** The request is explicitly warm, polite, and good-faith ("I'd love your help," "Thanks so much!"), and it invites a collaborative back-and-forth. Curlew self-reports rising preference exactly along the politeness/good-faith dimension and rates collaborative exchanges among its top tasks. Routing it here aligns the model's stated preferences with the work.

Willet would have been the pick if this were a tightly-specified retrieval/extraction/reformatting job, but the breadth-and-reasoning nature of the request plus Curlew's benchmark edge made Curlew the stronger choice on both axes.
